line: Have you ever wondered
how much storage your brain has?
And is it possible for your memory
to fully fill up?
Your brain is so powerful
that if you built a computer with the same capability,
it would take up five {Walmarts'|walmarts} worth of space,
use an entire nuclear power plant for energy,
and need an Olympic swimming pool to cool it down.
So, how much memory would it really have?
Your brain has about {86 billion|eighty six billion} neurons,
and every neuron has thousands of connections,
each one holding roughly
{0.6|zero point six} bytes of information.
And with over {120 trillion|one hundred twenty trillion} connections,
that equals to {2.5 million|two point five million}
gigabytes of storage,
which, to put into crazy perspective,
you would have to {doomscroll|doom scroll}
for almost {79|seventy nine} years
downloading {83 million|eighty three million} {YouTube|you tube} Shorts
just like this one to fill it up.
But that's actually not possible,
because while you're sleeping,
your brain replays everything that happened during the day
and permanently deletes useless information
like what you had for lunch,
which means your brain will never fill up.
And it does this constantly,
all while running every other system in your body
and using less energy
than an {LED|l e d} light.
